newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan April bad-cheque ratio falls to 0.55 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan April bad-cheque ratio falls to 0.55 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's bad-cheque ratio fell slightly to 0.55 percent in April from 0.56 percent in March, the central bank said in a statement on Thursday.
The number of bad cheques accounted for 0.55 percent of the total cheques written in April. The value of bad cheques represented 0.31 percent of the value of all cheques written, the bank said.
Taiwan's bad-cheque problems have been easing since the ratio hit a 10-year high of 0.80 percent in October 1995 amid a slumping economy.
In annual terms, 1995's 0.67 percent was also a 10-year peak, the highest since the ratio hit 0.75 percent in 1985.

The bank attributed the rising number of bad cheques in 1995 to the slow economy and Taiwan's slumping property and stock markets. But in recent months, the bad-cheque problems have eased gradually, it said.
